title: Nvidia sellers reportedly bar neoclouds from renting to Chinese firms
excerpt: Nvidia chip sellers have told neoclouds they won't supply GPUs if any capacity goes to Chinese firms, CNBC reports, after a new US chip rule.
content_html:
Sellers of Nvidia chips have told neoclouds they will not supply GPUs if any of the resulting capacity is rented to Chinese companies, CNBC reported. That is stricter than Nvidia’s earlier 50% limit and follows a US rule that took effect on November 19.

Companies that sell Nvidia chips have told neoclouds they will not supply GPUs if any of the computing power will be rented to Chinese companies, CNBC reported on Thursday. Neoclouds are firms that rent out AI computing capacity.

The report cited two people familiar with the matter. The condition goes further than Nvidia’s own line: it had said it would not sell to customers renting more than half their GPUs to Chinese firms.

The sellers’ messages followed a US rule that took effect on November 19. It requires licences for data centres abroad that give Chinese companies large amounts of computing power, closing a gap that let them rent top Nvidia chips they cannot buy.

Some sellers are already hunting for new buyers. Thousands of Nvidia B300s have gone up for sale since the rule took effect, many first meant for data centres serving Chinese firms. Asian data centres are now courting US buyers, and B300 rental prices have fallen about 7% in a month.

“Some rules were issued by the Commerce Department last week to close off indirect access,” US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer told CNBC. He pointed to smuggling through Southeast Asia and remote access from data centres in other countries.

China has threatened countermeasures over the rule. Nvidia and the Commerce Department did not immediately respond to CNBC.
